Paragraph: When Prince Bharata learned of the unjust exile of Rama and the death of King Dasaratha, he fell to the ground grieving deeply. Blaming his mother Kaikeyi, he refused the crown, expressing intense anger and self-reproach. Driven by deep love and responsibility, Bharata marched to Chitrakoot to beg Rama to return, willing to go into exile in Rama's place.
Situation/Problem_Faced: Overwhelming survivor guilt, familial betrayal, sudden loss, and moral shock upon realizing his mother caused Rama's exile.
Key_Teaching/Action_Taken: Bharata refuses to profit from unrighteousness, redirecting his grief into proactive duty (Svadharma) and selfless devotion.
Outcome/Resolution: Bharata channels his intense emotional distress into serving as a caretaker regent for Rama, maintaining integrity under extreme grief.

Spiritual_Psychological_Concept_Indian.Concept: Nishkama Seva (Selfless service to heal personal sorrow)
Bhakti (Devotion as a source of moral strength)
Tyaga (Sacrifice of self-interest for moral harmony)

Brief_Summary_Spiritual: Bharata exemplifies ultimate selflessness and moral duty, refusing to let another's unrighteousness compromise his devotion to Rama.
Brief_Summary_Psychological: Illustrates how processing trauma and moral injury can be facilitated by value-driven action and altruistic redirection.
